Revisiting the actuation tradeoff

After working with cycloidal joints, I began studying a lower-reduction planetary layout for quasi-direct-drive actuation.

The design work focuses on fitting the sun, planets, ring, bearings, and output structure into a compact motor package. Several gear candidates are retained in the CAD history as the geometry and interfaces evolve.

Start with the geometric relationships

For a simple planetary set, tooth counts and planet-center spacing need to be compatible with both gear meshes. Changing the carrier spacing affects the sun–planet and planet–ring interfaces together.

Compatible tooth counts
Nr = Ns + 2Np

For gears sharing the same module and standard pitch geometry, the ring tooth count Nr equals the sun tooth count Ns plus twice the planet tooth count Np.

Fixed ring · Sun input · Carrier output
G = 1 + Nr / Ns
PCDcarrier = m(Ns + Np)

G is the ideal speed-reduction ratio for this stated configuration. The carrier pitch-circle diameter follows from the module m and the sun–planet center distance. These are design relationships, not measured performance.

What I’m working through

  • Compare reduction candidates against the available motor and housing envelope.
  • Check planet placement and support, output interfaces, and assembly access.
  • Connect encoder and motor-controller packaging with the mechanical layout.
  • Keep candidate geometry distinct from a finalized, manufactured design.

Current stage

PROJECT STATUS

CAD geometry and packaging study.

The repository contains multiple gear candidates and actuator CAD. I have not established a finalized manufactured QDD ratio, a continuous torque rating, or validated strength and fatigue performance. The next steps are to settle the assembly, specify the manufacturing and material assumptions, then test a physical prototype.
